cards.text: Ahab, king of Israel, just watched the LORD hand him a big win over Ben-hadad, king of Aram. But Ben-hadad got away. Now the prophet comes back to Ahab, and friend, he is NOT here to throw a victory party.

cards.question: The prophet tells Ahab to strengthen his position, because in the ___ the king of Aram will come up against him.

cards.text: Meanwhile, over in Aram, Ben-hadad's servants are working out why they lost. And they decide it's all about the landscape.

cards.question: What do Ben-hadad's servants say about the gods of Israel?

answers.text: They are gods of the hills
They are gods of the rivers
They are gods of the desert

cards.question: So Ben-hadad's servants say the next fight with Israel should happen on the ___.

cards.text: Lose a battle, blame the hills. That's losing at checkers and blaming the TABLE.
The plan keeps going: dismiss all the kings from their positions and replace them with officers. The whole management team, GONE.

cards.question: What kind of army do Ben-hadad's servants tell him to raise?

answers.text: One just like the army he lost
One twice the size of the last
A smaller army that moves faster

cards.question: Ben-hadad turns down his servants' plan.

cards.text: Nope. He approves it and does it all, horse for horse and chariot for chariot. Then in the spring, right when the prophet said, Ben-hadad mobilizes the Arameans to fight Israel.

cards.question: Ben-hadad goes up to ___ to fight against Israel.

cards.text: Israel mobilizes too. They gather supplies and march out to meet Aram, and the text paints a picture of the two camps.

cards.question: The Israelites camp like two small flocks of goats. What does the Aramean army look like?

answers.text: It fits in one small valley
It hides behind the city walls

cards.text: Two little flocks of GOATS against the whole countryside. That's me showing up to tug-of-war alone on my gold base, and the other side brought a whole TOWN.
Then the man of God comes to Ahab with a word from the LORD. The Arameans have said the LORD is a god of the hills and not of the valleys, and He heard them.

cards.question: What does the LORD say He will do because of what the Arameans said about Him?

answers.text: Deliver their great army into Ahab's hand
Let the Arameans win on the plains
Send a storm to scatter both armies

cards.text: For seven days the two armies just camp across from each other. Seven DAYS of the world's longest staring contest.

cards.question: On the seventh day, the battle comes, and Israel strikes down the Arameans.

cards.text: The Arameans who are left run into the city of Aphek. And then the wall falls on twenty-seven thousand of them.

cards.question: Ben-hadad runs into Aphek too, and he hides in an inner ___.

cards.text: Ben-hadad's servants come to him in his hiding spot. They've heard something about the kings of Israel that gives them a little hope.

cards.question: What have Ben-hadad's servants heard about the kings of the house of Israel?
So Ben-hadad's servants plan to go out to Ahab with ___ around their waists and ___ around their heads.

cards.text: They're hoping Ahab will spare Ben-hadad's life. So out they go to Ahab with the message: Ben-hadad says, "Please spare my life."

cards.question: Ahab, king of Israel, hears that Ben-hadad is still alive. What does Ahab call him?

cards.text: His BROTHER? Brother?! Friend, these two kings have gone to war TWICE.

cards.question: Ben-hadad's servants hear Ahab say brother and decide to stay quiet.

cards.text: Ahab says, "Go and get him!" So Ben-hadad goes from hiding in an inner room to riding in Ahab's own CHARIOT.

cards.question: Riding in Ahab's chariot, what does Ben-hadad promise him?

answers.text: To restore the cities his father took
To send his son to live in Samaria
To hand over all of his chariots

cards.question: Ben-hadad also says Ahab can set up his own marketplaces in Damascus.
So what does Ahab do with Ben-hadad, king of Aram?

answers.text: Makes a treaty and sends him away
Keeps him as a prisoner in Samaria
Hands him over to the man of God

cards.text: Ben-hadad rides off free with a treaty. Sounds like a happy ending, but hang on, friend.
Meanwhile, by the word of the LORD, one of the sons of the prophets turns to his companion. And he has a VERY strange request.

cards.question: What does this prophet ask his companion to do?
The prophet's companion does what the prophet asks.

cards.text: Honestly? If somebody walked into my bakery saying "Strike me, please!" I'd say no too. But this came by the word of the LORD, and the prophet tells him he has not obeyed the voice of the LORD.

cards.question: The prophet says that as soon as his companion leaves him, a ___ will kill him.

cards.text: And when the man leaves, a lion finds him and kills him.
So the prophet finds another man and says that line again: "Strike me, please!"

cards.question: This second man strikes the prophet and wounds him.

cards.text: Wounded, the prophet goes and waits on the road for the king. And he's in disguise.

cards.question: How does the prophet disguise himself while he waits for the king?

answers.text: With a bandage over his eyes
With a long cloak and hood

cards.text: When the king passes by, the prophet cries out to him with a story from the middle of the battle.

cards.question: In the prophet's story, a man brought him a captive and told him to guard him.
In the prophet's story, what would it cost him if that captive went missing?

answers.text: His life or a talent of silver
His house and all his land

cards.text: Then the prophet says that while he was busy here and there, the man disappeared. Busy here and there, friend? I've said those EXACT words to a burnt batch.

cards.question: Ahab tells the prophet he can go free this time.

cards.text: Ahab tells him he has pronounced his own judgment. Then the prophet quickly pulls off the bandage, and Ahab recognizes him as one of the prophets.

cards.question: Now the prophet gives Ahab a word from the LORD. What did Ahab let slip from his hand?

answers.text: The man God had devoted to destruction
The cities Aram took from his father
The silver his army won in battle

cards.question: The LORD says Ahab's ___ will be exchanged for Ben-hadad's life, and Ahab's ___ for Ben-hadad's people.

cards.text: Sullen and angry, the king of Israel goes home to Samaria. We'll leave him there for now, friend, but Ahab's story is far from done.

findings.problem: The card states facts from before the passage: the LORD handed Ahab a big win over Ben-hadad, and Ben-hadad got away (1 Kings 20:13-21, especially 20:20-21). It cites only 1 Kings 20:22, so those facts have no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about the servants' reasoning from 20:23, which cards 3 to 5 already covered. It tells no new part of the passage and does not move it forward. The joke should ride on a card that tells the passage, like card 7.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "It hides behind the city walls" is true later in the passage. The Arameans who are left flee into the city of Aphek (1 Kings 20:30), and Ben-hadad hides there too. A baker could argue this answer is right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: This story card is only the tug-of-war joke about the goats and the countryside, which card 13 already covered. It tells no new part of the passage. The joke should ride on a card that moves the passage, like card 12 or card 15.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The LORD's reason and purpose in 1 Kings 20:28, "Then you will know that I am the LORD," is never told or asked anywhere in the walkthrough. It is the point of the battle and of the rebuke that follows.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The size of the victory in 1 Kings 20:29, a hundred thousand foot soldiers in one day, is never told. It shows the LORD keeping His word to deliver "all this great army." The stop ends on the true or false card and never tells the result.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card is only a reaction to the answer on card 7 and tells no new part of the passage. It also states a fact from outside its citation: these two kings have gone to war twice (1 Kings 20:1 and 20:26). The card cites only 1 Kings 20:32.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: After card 9 shows that the servants don't stay quiet, no card tells what they actually do in 1 Kings 20:33: they were looking for a sign of hope, quickly grasped at the word, and replied, "Yes, your brother Ben-hadad." Card 10 jumps straight to "Go and get him!"

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The first sentence only restates the answer to card 13, that Ben-hadad goes free with a treaty. That makes this a recap card. It also adds "rides off," while the text says Ahab "sent him away" (1 Kings 20:34).

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The question says "this prophet" and points back to a story card the baker can no longer see. It should say who he is, for example one of the sons of the prophets.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "Honestly?", the bakery joke, and the line about the word of the LORD.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says "This second man" and points back to the story card before it, which is no longer on screen. It should give the context, for example the second man the prophet asks to strike him.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the retelling, "Busy here and there, friend?", and the burnt batch joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer uses the distinctive Bible phrase "devoted to destruction." The wrong answers are plain everyday wording, so the right answer stands out by sounding more like the Bible.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
